The token is checked and saved, and the bot can be used at once. Call it after the user created the bot (setup_check has the steps).

tools.name: enable_tools
tools.description: Turn on more Discord tools for this conversation. Only the core tools are on at first; call this as soon as a task needs one of these packs: automations (role menus, welcome messages with auto-roles, support tickets and their history, the server's own slash commands, staff slash commands (/ban, /lock, /purge…), moderation logs and searching them, staff alerts, support forums, rules (when X happens do Y), member verification, scheduled messages); live (what is happening now, waiting for a reply, mention or join); jobs (background jobs: message backups and restores, roles for many members at once); moderation (AutoMod, locking channels, purging messages, bans list, pruning, audit log, role audit, member export); messaging (webhooks (post with another name), DMs, pins list, announcements publishing, polls and reactions results); organizing (cloning channels, more forum tags, threads, following announcement channels, copying and syncing permissions); server_settings (onboarding, welcome screen, invites list, server stats and activity, bot profile, creating or leaving servers); expressions (emojis, stickers, soundboard, scheduled events, stage, application commands); api (direct Discord API calls for anything else).

instructions: Tools to manage Discord servers through one or more bots. Start with setup_check (bots, their servers, what to fix); new bots are added with add_bot, which asks for the token in a private box (never ask for it in chat). Tools use the bot that is in the server you name. Call get_server before changing a server. Channels, roles and members can be named instead of using ids. Before changing the server or sending messages, show the user what will happen and get their confirmation; deleting is permanent. Nobody is pinged unless ping_roles/ping_users/ping_everyone are set. Every write tool accepts dry_run to preview; permanent actions need confirm: true. To build or complete a server show preview_blueprint, then apply_blueprint. Only the core tools are on at first: when a task needs more (role menus, welcomes, tickets, live events, background jobs and backups, AutoMod and moderation, webhooks and DMs, emojis, scheduled events, onboarding, raw API calls), call enable_tools with the pack first; if the new tools do not appear, call them through use_tool. Role menus, welcomes and tickets keep working while this server runs. Set up only the features the user chose, with the options they chose; when a feature has variants (where a log goes, which commands, who gets alerts), ask before building, and show the plan first.
